title: Finite separable residue extensions lift to finite etale Cohen extensions
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $D$ be a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], with residue field $F=D/pD$. Let $L/F$ be a finite separable field extension [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], where finite means finite-dimensional as an $F$-vector space. Then there are a Cohen ring $B$, an injective local ring homomorphism $i:D\to B$, and an isomorphism $e:B/pB\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ identifying the residue map of $i$ with the specified inclusion $F\to L$, such that $i$ is finite etale. Here finite etale means that $B$ is a finitely generated $D$-module and $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Reduction induces a bijection $\operatorname{Aut}_D(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Aut}_F(L)$; these are the groups of ring automorphisms fixing the indicated base pointwise, and the residue automorphism is transported by $e$.

proof.text: The Cohen-ring definition gives a local DVR $D$, maximal ideal $pD$, complete for that ideal. Apply lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian to $(D,pD)$; by the henselian terminology $D$ is a henselian local ring. Apply lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-field-lift to the specified finite separable extension $L/F$. Obtain a finite etale $D$-algebra $B$ and an $F$-algebra isomorphism $e:B/pB\cong L$, using $(D/pD)\otimes_D B\cong B/pB$. This quotient identification sends $\bar a\otimes b$ to $i(a)b\bmod pB$, with inverse $\bar b\mapsto1\otimes b$; changing a representative by a multiple of $p$ has zero image. Thus $e$ respects the specified inclusion $F\to L$.

source.place: Tag 0ALJ, lemma-complete-henselian; algebra.tex Tag 04GK, lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale, final paragraph

proof.text: Since $i$ is etale, lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat makes $B$ a flat $D$-module. It is finitely generated by the finite clause of the lift. Hence lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free supplies a $D$-basis. This basis is finite: write a finite generating set in basis coordinates; the union of its finite supports contains every basis index, since otherwise that basis vector could not be generated. The basis is nonempty because $B/pB\cong L$ is a nonzero field. Thus $B$ is free of finite positive rank over $D$.

Apply lem-sfb-finite-free-field-fibre-dvr to $A=D$, uniformizer $p$, and $B$: Step 2 gives the finite nonempty basis, and Step 1 gives the nonzero field quotient. Therefore $i$ is injective, $B$ is a DVR, and its maximal ideal is $pB$. The homomorphism $i$ is local: its induced residue map $F\to B/pB$ is the inclusion $F\to L$ transported through $e$, so $i(d)\in pB$ if and only if $d\in pD$.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, uniformizer characterization; more-algebra.tex Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, p-base preparation

proof.text: The PID $D$ is Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal. It is complete local by Step 1, and $B$ is a finite $D$-algebra and a domain by Steps 1 and 3. The domain clause of lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product makes $B$ complete for its maximal ideal. That ideal is $pB$ by Step 3. The Cohen-ring definition now applies to $B$ with the same prime $p$: it is a DVR complete for $pB$ and with uniformizer $p$. The finiteness, etaleness, and specified residue identification remain those of Step 1.

Apply lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-map-bijective with $R=D$ and $S=T=B$. Given $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}_F(L)$, lift $e^{-1}\alpha e$ uniquely to a $D$-algebra endomorphism $u$ of $B$; lift $e^{-1}\alpha^{-1}e$ to $v$. Both $uv$ and $vu$ reduce to the identity of $B/pB$, so injectivity of the same Hom-set reduction gives $uv=vu=\mathrm{id}_B$. Thus $u$ is a $D$-automorphism. Conversely every $D$-automorphism preserves $pB$, and reduction is injective by that Hom-set bijection. Reduction followed by conjugation by $e$ is therefore the asserted bijection of automorphism groups; it respects composition because residue maps and conjugation do.
